categories.main_business_segments: U-Haul Holding Company operates through three primary segments: Moving and Storage, Property and Casualty Insurance, and Life Insurance. The Moving and Storage segment includes truck and trailer rentals, self-storage, portable storage (U-Box), and sales of moving supplies and towing accessories. Property and Casualty Insurance provides insurance products and claims handling for U-Haul customers, while the Life Insurance segment focuses on life, health, and annuity products for the senior market.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: U-Haul designs and manufactures its own van boxes and trailers at company-operated facilities, integrating proprietary features such as the Lowest Deck, Gentle Ride Suspension, and Mom’s Attic for ease of use and safety. The company leverages a proprietary reservations management system for real-time inventory tracking and utilizes web-based platforms and mobile apps for customer engagement, self-service rentals, and marketplace connections. Preventive maintenance and sustainability practices are embedded in equipment design and operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are 'do-it-yourself' movers, including individuals, families, college students, and small businesses needing moving and storage solutions. U-Haul also serves commercial customers, independent dealers, and the senior market through its insurance products. The company targets both residential and commercial end markets for moving, storage, and insurance services.
categories.geographic_coverage: U-Haul operates across all 50 U.S. states and 10 Canadian provinces, with nearly 2,400 company-operated retail locations and over 21,600 independent dealers. The company also manages over 2,000 self-storage locations and has a significant presence in both urban and rural areas throughout North America.
categories.supply_chain_position: U-Haul operates primarily at the downstream end of the supply chain, directly serving end customers through rentals, sales, and services. It also manages a large network of independent dealers and storage affiliates, and maintains upstream activities through its in-house manufacturing and assembly of rental equipment.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the dealer and affiliate network, increasing the rental fleet and storage capacity, enhancing digital platforms (including the U-Haul app and online marketplaces), and investing in sustainability and equipment innovation. The company is focused on customer convenience, operational efficiency, and adapting to regulatory and technological changes, such as electric vehicle integration and cybersecurity.
categories.revenue_model: U-Haul generates revenue primarily through rental fees for trucks, trailers, and self-storage units, sales of moving and storage products, commissions from independent dealers, and insurance premiums. Additional revenue streams include property management fees, propane sales, and investment income from insurance operations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors in truck rental include Avis Budget Group (Budget Truck Rental), Penske Truck Leasing, and Enterprise Truck Rental, while self-storage competitors include Public Storage, CubeSmart, and Extra Space Storage. U-Haul is the market leader in North American do-it-yourself moving and storage, with a broad geographic footprint and the largest rental fleet and dealer network.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, U-Haul reported consolidated revenues of $5.83 billion and net earnings of $367 million. The company maintains a large asset base ($20.5 billion), significant cash reserves, and a high level of capital expenditures, particularly in fleet and real estate. While revenue and storage occupancy grew year-over-year, earnings declined due to higher costs and depreciation, reflecting ongoing investment and competitive pressures.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: U-Haul emphasizes convenience, nationwide coverage, and a comprehensive 'one-stop' solution for moving and storage needs. Differentiators include proprietary equipment features (Lowest Deck, Gentle Ride Suspension), extensive dealer and affiliate networks, digital self-service options (Truck Share 24/7), and integrated insurance offerings. The brand is recognized for reliability, affordability, and sustainability through equipment sharing and operational efficiencies.
